chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Yaqub al-Ahmar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'There is a heavy debt upon me, and what has come upon me has caused the Quran to slip away from me.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Quran! The Quran! Verily the verse from the Quran and the chapter shall come on the Day of Resurrection until it ascends a thousand levels — meaning in Paradise — and it shall say: Had you memorized me, I would have brought you here.'

key_terms.حَفِظَ: To memorize / to preserve / to guard — the Quranic concept of hifz encompasses both intellectual memorization and protective custody
key_terms.دَرَجَة: Level / degree / rank — refers to the hierarchical stations in Paradise, with each memorized verse elevating both itself and its memorizer
key_terms.يَتَفَلَّتُ: Slips away / escapes from memory — the root f-l-t conveys something that breaks free uncontrollably, here used for Quranic verses escaping from a distressed mind

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about forgetting the Quran due to worldly worries?
ai.summary: Yaqub al-Ahmar reported that he complained to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about his heavy debts causing him to forget the Quran. The Imam responded with an urgent exhortation to maintain the Quran, vividly describing how on the Day of Resurrection, individual Quranic verses and chapters will personally ascend a thousand levels in Paradise and lament to their memorizer: 'Had you preserved me in your memory, I would have carried you to this lofty station.' This hadith was addressed to someone whose worldly troubles — heavy debt and anxiety — were causing spiritual neglect, and the Imam redirected his concern from temporal distress to eternal consequence.
